proofs.proof_tex:
Assume the rational empirical input and rational \(0<\epsilon<1\) required by the statement. Set
\[
M=\left\lceil\frac{32d}{\epsilon}\right\rceil,
\qquad h=M^{-1},
\qquad \eta=3dh.
\tag{13}
\]
Then \(M\) is a positive integer, \(h\) and \(\eta\) are rational,
\[
0<h\le\frac{\epsilon}{32d},
\qquad
M\le\frac{32d}{\epsilon}+1,
\tag{14}
\]
and all of these quantities have encoding length polynomial in the encoding length of \(\epsilon\) and \(d\).

Round each coordinate of an empirical atom \(x\) to a multiple of \(h\), with a deterministic tie rule, and denote the result by \(q(x)\). Coordinatewise rounding gives \(|q_j(x)-x_j|\le h\) for \(j=1,\ldots,d\). Since \(d\ge1\),
\[
\|q(x)-x\|_2
\le\sum_{j=1}^d|q_j(x)-x_j|
\le dh.
\tag{15}
\]
This deliberately rational bound avoids introducing \(\sqrt d\) into the certificate. For a tuple \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_K)\), define
\[
a=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^Kx_k,
\qquad
a_q=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^Kq(x_k).
\]
Unit-ball support gives \(\|a\|_2\le1\); (15) gives \(\|a-a_q\|_2\le dh\), and hence \(\|a_q\|_2\le1+dh\). By (14), \(dh\le\epsilon/32<1/32\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
|c_K(x)-c_K(q(x))|
&=|\|a\|_2^2-\|a_q\|_2^2|\\
&\le\|a-a_q\|_2(\|a\|_2+\|a_q\|_2)\\
&\le dh(2+dh)\\
&\le3dh=\eta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
Every quantity on the final line is rational.

Merge atoms in each arm that have the same quantized image. Write the distinct images as \(q_{kj}\) and their rational empirical masses as \(\widehat p_{kj}\). The gridded dual linear program is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{maximize}\quad&\sum_{k,j}\widehat p_{kj}u_{kj},\\
\text{subject to}\quad&\sum_{k=1}^Ku_{k j_k}
\le K^{-2}\left\|\sum_{k=1}^Kq_{k j_k}\right\|_2^2
\quad\text{for every }(j_1,\ldots,j_K).
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Its coefficients are rational. To separate a proposed rational vector \(u\), define \(D_0(0)=0\), set all other nonexistent states to \(+\infty\), and recursively compute
\[
D_k(s)=\min_{j_1,\ldots,j_k:\,\sum_{\ell=1}^kq_{\ell j_\ell}=s}
\left(-\sum_{\ell=1}^ku_{\ell j_\ell}\right).
\tag{18}
\]
Equivalently, each transition updates
\[
D_k(s+q_{kj})
=\min\{D_k(s+q_{kj}),D_{k-1}(s)-u_{kj}\}.
\]
At the final layer,
\[
\min_s\left\{D_K(s)+K^{-2}\|s\|_2^2\right\}
=\min_{j_1,\ldots,j_K}
\left\{K^{-2}\left\|\sum_kq_{k j_k}\right\|_2^2-\sum_ku_{k j_k}\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
A negative minimizer supplies a violated constraint of (17), while a nonnegative minimum certifies every constraint. Thus (18)--(19) are an exact strong separation oracle, not a relaxation.

Every coordinate of \(q_{kj}\) is a multiple of \(h\) and has absolute value at most \(1+h\). A partial sum therefore has each coordinate in an interval of length at most \(2K(1+h)\). From (14), the number of partial-sum states at a layer is at most
\[
O_d((K/h)^d)=O_d((K/\epsilon)^d).
\tag{20}
\]
There are at most \(m\) transitions out of a state at each of the \(K\) layers. The balanced identity \(N=Km\) therefore bounds the total number of dynamic-programming transitions by \(O_d(N(K/\epsilon)^d)\). Exact additions and comparisons involve rational numbers of polynomial encoding length.

We next verify the boundedness premise needed for oracle-polynomial optimization. The quantized points satisfy \(\|q_{kj}\|_2\le1+dh<2\), so every cost in (17) lies in \([0,4]\). The product of the gridded marginals is a feasible primal coupling, and its bounded cost gives a finite primal optimum. Lemma~\texttt{lem:finite-lp-optimization} therefore supplies finite primal and dual optimizers with equal values. Starting from an optimal dual, replace one potential at a time by its finite \(c_K\)-transform
\[
u_k(q_{kj})
=\min_{(j_\ell)_{\ell\ne k}}
\left\{c_K(q_{1j_1},\ldots,q_{Kj_K})-
\sum_{\ell\ne k}u_\ell(q_{\ell j_\ell})\right\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Feasibility of the old tuple implies that (21) can only increase \(u_k\); the new tuple is feasible by its definition. Since the old tuple is optimal and all marginal masses are nonnegative and sum to one, the objective cannot increase strictly. Thus sequential application of (21) preserves optimality. For any two support points \(q,q'\) in margin \(k\), the elementary inequality \(|\inf A-\inf B|\le\sup|A-B|\) and the cost range give
\[
|u_k(q)-u_k(q')|
\le\sup_{q_{-k}}|c_K(q,q_{-k})-c_K(q',q_{-k})|
\le4.
\tag{22}
\]

Choose one reference point in every nonempty marginal support. Gauge shifts \(u_k\mapsto u_k+b_k\) with \(\sum_kb_k=0\) preserve both feasibility and objective. Use them to make the first \(K-1\) reference values zero. Equation (22) then bounds all values in those margins by \(4\) in absolute value. The constraint at the all-reference tuple bounds the last reference value above by \(4\). Conversely, the zero dual is feasible, so the optimal value is nonnegative. The first \(K-1\) marginal integrals are at most \(4(K-1)\), and the last marginal integral is at most its reference value plus \(4\). Hence optimality implies
\[
0\le\sum_{k,j}\widehat p_{kj}u_{kj}
\le4(K-1)+u_K(q_{K0})+4,
\]
so \(u_K(q_{K0})\ge-4K\). Together with (22), this places an optimal dual in a rational box of radius \(4K+4\), whose encoding length is polynomial.

Lemma~\texttt{lem:finite-lp-optimization}, applied to (17), this rational box, and the oracle (18)--(19), now computes an optimal gridded dual value \(L_g\) and recovers a primal optimizer with the same value and finite rational witnesses. Its running time is polynomial in the input bit length, \(N\), and the state bound (20).

Push any coupling of the original empirical laws forward coordinatewise through \(q\). This gives a feasible gridded coupling, and (16) changes its objective by at most \(\eta\). Conversely, lift the gridded primal optimizer by drawing, conditional on each quantized tuple, each original coordinate from the corresponding empirical quantization fiber with its empirical conditional probabilities. This preserves every original empirical marginal, and (16) again changes the objective by at most \(\eta\). Taking the respective infima gives
\[
L_g-\eta\le L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\le L_g+\eta.
\tag{23}
\]
The lifted primal is an explicit certificate for the upper inequality. If \(u\) is the gridded dual witness, compose every potential with \(q\) on the original atoms and subtract \(\eta\) from the first potential. By (16) and (17), for every original tuple \(x\),
\[
\sum_{k=1}^Ku_k(q(x_k))-\eta
\le c_K(q(x))-\eta
\le c_K(x).
\]
Thus these shifted potentials are dual feasible for the original empirical problem and have objective \(L_g-\eta\), certifying the lower inequality in (23).

Return
\[
\underline L_\epsilon=L_g-\eta,
\qquad
\overline L_\epsilon=L_g+\eta.
\]
Equations (13)--(14) give the rational width bound
\[
\overline L_\epsilon-\underline L_\epsilon
=2\eta=6dh\le\frac{3}{16}\epsilon<\epsilon.
\]
This proves the stated bracket, witnesses, rational auditability, and complexity bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let
\[
q_d=\min\left\{\frac14,\frac{d-4}{2(d-2)}\right\}.
\]
For fixed \(d>4\), there are constants \(0<c_d\le C_d<\infty\) and \(c_0>0\) such that, whenever \(N=Km\), \(K\ge3\), and \(m\ge2\),
\[
c_dN^{-1/2}\le R_d(N,K)
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
Consequently, uniformly along every legal triangular array satisfying \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), one has \(R_d(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\). In particular, \(q_5=1/6\), whereas \(q_d=1/4\) for every \(d\ge6\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose the data-driven estimator \(T=\widehat L\). By Theorem~\texttt{thm:improved-plugin-upper}, under balanced armwise product sampling and unit-ball support there is a finite constant \(C_d\), depending only on the fixed dimension, such that
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\tag{1}
\]
The infimum over all measurable estimators in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk} is no larger than the risk of this one estimator, so (1) proves the asserted upper bound.

For the converse, invoke Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}. It supplies two laws \(\mathbf P^{(0)}\) and \(\mathbf P^{(1)}\) in the maintained arbitrary-margin class such that, writing \(L_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)})\) and \(\Delta=L_1-L_0\),
\[
\Delta\ge aN^{-1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\le\frac14,
\tag{2}
\]
where \(\mathbb P_j=\bigotimes_{k=1}^K(P_k^{(j)})^{\otimes m}\) is the observable product law. Fix any measurable estimator \(T\), and define the test
\[
\phi=\mathbf 1\left\{T>\frac{L_0+L_1}{2}\right\}.
\]
On \(\{\phi=1\}\), \(|T-L_0|\ge\Delta/2\), while on \(\{\phi=0\}\), \(|T-L_1|\ge\Delta/2\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_j|T-L_j|
&\ge \frac12\left(\mathbb E_0|T-L_0|+\mathbb E_1|T-L_1|\right)\\
&\ge \frac{\Delta}{4}\{\mathbb P_0(\phi=1)+\mathbb P_1(\phi=0)\}\\
&\ge \frac{\Delta}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\}\\
&\ge \frac{3a}{16}N^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The third line follows directly from \(\mathbb P_1(\phi=1)-\mathbb P_0(\phi=1)\le\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\). Taking first the supremum over \(\mathbf P\) and then the infimum over \(T\) proves the lower bound with \(c_d=3a/16\); the constant is universal and therefore may be indexed by \(d\).

It remains to locate the elbow. The second term in the minimum in (1) can be rewritten, using the positive identity \(m=N/K\), as
\[
\frac1K m^{-2/d}=N^{-2/d}K^{-(d-2)/d}.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(d=5\), then \(q_d=(d-4)/\{2(d-2)\}=1/6\). Thus \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) and (4) give
\[
N^{-2/d}K^{-(d-2)/d}
\le c_0^{-(d-2)/d}
N^{-2/d-q_d(d-2)/d}
=c_0^{-(d-2)/d}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(d\ge6\), then \((d-4)/\{2(d-2)\}\ge1/4\), so \(q_d=1/4\). Since \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\), the other member of the minimum satisfies
\[
\frac r{K^2}\le \frac d{c_0^2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (5) and (6), each used only in its indicated dimension regime, show that the minimum in (1) is bounded by a dimension-dependent multiple of \(N^{-1/2}\). Combining this fact with (3) proves \(R_d(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\). The condition \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\) only identifies the legal limiting arrays; all inequalities above are finite-sample and uniform, so no interchange of limits is used.
added_lemmas.justification: The improved empirical term yields a dimension-dependent root-\(N\) elbow, while the Bernoulli experiment retains the all-estimator converse.
added_lemmas.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Gao--Ge--Qian do not establish this growing-arm root-\(N\) region; their published model is broader in \(d\) and permits \(K=2\).
added_lemmas.consumer: It removes every array with \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\) from the unresolved minimax frontier.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(q_d=\min\{1/4,(d-4)/[2(d-2)]\}\), and let \(U_{N,K}\) and \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) be defined in Definition~\texttt{def:plugin-lower-bound}. For fixed \(d>4\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\),
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha
\]
and there are constants \(0<c_{d,\alpha}\le C_{d,\alpha}<\infty\) such that
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
Consequently \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) uniformly along every legal array satisfying \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\); here \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). No matching nonparametric expected-length converse is asserted for smaller \(K\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let
\[
U_{N,K}=C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right],
\qquad u_{N,K}=\frac{U_{N,K}}{\alpha},
\]
where \(C_d\) is chosen so that Theorem~\texttt{thm:improved-plugin-upper} yields
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|\le U_{N,K}.
\tag{7}
\]
The quantity \(U_{N,K}\) is strictly positive because \(C_d>0\) and \(N^{-1/2}>0\). For every nonnegative \(Y\) and positive \(u\), the pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{Y>u\}\le Y/u\) gives \(\Pr(Y>u)\le\mathbb EY/u\) after integration. Applying this derived inequality with \(Y=|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|\) and then using (7) gives, for every \(\mathbf P\),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\left\{|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|>u_{N,K}\right\}
\le \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|}{u_{N,K}}
\le\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]
On the complementary event, \(\widehat L-u_{N,K}\le L(\mathbf P)\). The squared-sum cost is nonnegative, so its infimum satisfies \(L(\mathbf P)\ge0\). Consequently
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}
=\max\{0,\widehat L-u_{N,K}\}
\le L(\mathbf P)
\tag{9}
\]
on that event. Equations (8)--(9) imply
\[
\inf_{\mathbf P}\Pr_{\mathbf P}\{B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\le L(\mathbf P)\}\ge1-\alpha,
\]
which is exactly \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) by Definition~\texttt{def:honest-bounds}.

For length, the definition of the maximum gives \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\ge\widehat L-u_{N,K}\). Hence, pointwise,
\[
\begin{aligned}
[L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}]_+
&\le[L(\mathbf P)-\widehat L+u_{N,K}]_+\\
&\le|L(\mathbf P)-\widehat L|+u_{N,K}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking expectations and using (7) yields
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{plug}})_+]
\le(1+\alpha^{-1})U_{N,K}.
\tag{10}
\]
Since Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length} takes the infimum over all honest lower bounds and (9) proves that this particular bound is honest, (10) proves the asserted upper bound after absorbing \(1+\alpha^{-1}\) into \(C_{d,\alpha}\).

For the converse, take the ordered pair in Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}. With the notation of (2), \(L_1-L_0=\Delta\ge aN^{-1/2}\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\le1/4\). Let \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) be arbitrary. Honesty at the low-endpoint law and the defining total-variation inequality imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_1(B_N\le L_0)
&\ge \mathbb P_0(B_N\le L_0)-\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\\
&\ge1-\alpha-\frac14>\frac12,
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where the strict final inequality uses the declared condition \(\alpha<1/4\). On \(\{B_N\le L_0\}\),
\[
[L_1-B_N]_+\ge L_1-L_0=\Delta.
\]
Thus (11) gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+]
\ge\mathbb E_1[(L_1-B_N)_+]
\ge\frac{a}{2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) proves the lower bound.

Finally, use \(m=N/K\). If \(d=5\), then \(q_d=1/6\), and \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) gives
\[
K^{-1}m^{-2/d}=N^{-2/d}K^{-(d-2)/d}
\le c_0^{-(d-2)/d}N^{-1/2}.
\]
If \(d\ge6\), then \(q_d=1/4\), and \(r\le d\) gives
\[
r/K^2\le dc_0^{-2}N^{-1/2}.
\]
Thus in either dimension regime the minimum in \(U_{N,K}\) is \(O_d(N^{-1/2})\) whenever \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\). Combining this calculation with (10) and (12) proves the root-\(N\) conclusion. Because (12) uses only the Bernoulli pair, it proves no smaller-arm nonparametric converse, as the statement explicitly records.
added_lemmas.justification: Markov calibration converts the uniform mean plug-in risk into an explicit uniformly honest lower endpoint and an expected-length upper bound of the same order.
added_lemmas.gap: The ordered Bernoulli pair proves the root-\(N\) converse, but no smaller-arm nonparametric expected-length converse is claimed.
added_lemmas.consumer: A computed empirical endpoint can be reported with separate sampling and numerical error allowances.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Along legal arrays with \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), determine whether the jointly normalized class \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\) admits an aggregate localized empirical-process bound, uniform over \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), whose explicit \(K\)- and logarithmic order is strictly smaller than the present \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) contribution to the endpoint risk. A positive answer must give a computable two-sided localization bound for the sum of all \(K\) marginal dual fluctuations. A negative answer must instead instantiate the rational family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) with an endpoint separation of the corresponding order, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) against every rematching column, with strict slack off the declared contact columns. The currently defined search template is not asserted to establish either answer.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original dichotomy ranged over already settled large-arm arrays and could be read as suggesting that the uninstantiated finite search template supports one of its two outcomes. The proposed question is restricted to the unresolved \(K=o(N^{q_d})\) regime and asks exactly whether aggregate jointly conjugate localization can improve the current \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) term, with an explicit lower certificate required for a negative answer.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Along legal triangular arrays satisfying \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\) to determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) such that \(R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\), including the exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition inside this remaining regime. The estimation converse must instantiate a simultaneous finite-support family whose endpoint separation matches \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}\), whose hypothesis mixtures satisfy \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and whose reduced costs satisfy \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) for every alternative rematching. The expected-length converse must additionally order its low- and high-endpoint mixtures so that the same indistinguishability argument is one-sided. The upper branch must give a computable estimator and uniformly honest lower bound at the claimed rates, or replace the present \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) term by a proved sharper aggregate jointly conjugate complexity bound.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original all-\(K\) question includes the now-settled root-\(N\) region. The proposed claim removes that solved region and retains only the genuine \(K=o(N^{q_d})\) estimation and ordered one-sided gaps, including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and all-rematching certification.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Let \(M=\lceil32d/\epsilon\rceil\), let \(h=M^{-1}\), and round every coordinate of every empirical atom to a multiple of the rational mesh \(h\), using a fixed tie rule. Thus the quantization map \(q\) is rational and satisfies \(|q_j(x)-x_j|\le h\) in every coordinate and \(\|q(x)-x\|_2\le dh\). Put the rational allowance \(\eta=3dh\). The procedure \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) merges coincident quantized atoms, solves the resulting rational dual linear program by the ellipsoid method using exact dynamic-programming separation indexed by partial grid sums, recovers an optimal rational primal witness, lifts that witness through the quantization fibers, and returns the lifted-primal upper certificate and the shifted-dual lower certificate with allowance \(\eta\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The prior construction used \(\sqrt d\,h\) and a generally irrational cost allowance. The corrected construction uses the rational Euclidean-error upper bound \(dh\), the rational mesh \(h=1/\lceil32d/\epsilon\rceil\), and the rational allowance \(3dh\) while preserving \(O_d((K/\epsilon)^d)\) states.

proposed.name: Uniformly calibrated plug-in lower confidence bound
proposed.construction:
Fix a constant \(C_d<\infty\) for which Theorem~\texttt{thm:improved-plugin-upper} gives its uniform mean absolute-error bound, and set
\[
U_{N,K}=C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right],
\qquad
B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}=\max\left\{0,\widehat L-\frac{U_{N,K}}{\alpha}\right\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The sharper honest construction is a genuinely new empirical-MOT plug-in rule, not a correction of the valid but weaker mean-floor rule.
After deletion of the weaker mean-floor length theorem, the old construction is obsolete and has no remaining live formal reference; the new plug-in definition is the load-bearing honest procedure.
The \(N^{1/4}\) theorem is obsolete because the already-proved \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) term yields the sharper exponent \(q_d\), including \(q_5=1/6\).
The mean-floor theorem is obsolete after the plug-in construction attains the full improved upper rate and the sharper dimension-dependent elbow.

proposed.statement: Along legal arrays with \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), determine whether the jointly normalized class \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\) admits an aggregate localized empirical-process bound, uniform over \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), whose explicit \(K\)- and logarithmic order is strictly smaller than the present \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) contribution to the endpoint risk. A positive answer must give a computable two-sided localization bound for the sum of all \(K\) marginal dual fluctuations. A negative answer must instead instantiate the rational family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) with an endpoint separation of the corresponding order, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) against every rematching column, with strict slack off the declared contact columns. The currently defined search template is not asserted to establish either answer.
proposed.justification: The aggregate jointly conjugate fluctuation is the precise upper-side alternative to a simultaneous all-rematching lower construction in the unresolved small-arm region.
proposed.gap: No supplied theorem controls the sum of all \(K\) localized potentials, and the finite-support family has not been instantiated with simultaneous separation, mixture indistinguishability, and rematching resistance.
proposed.consumer: Its resolution decides whether the current \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) contribution can be reduced or must appear in a matching lower frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: For \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), either prove a computable aggregate localized complexity bound strictly sharper than \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\), with explicit logarithms, or construct the matching simultaneous finite-support family with \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\) and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) for every rematching column.
obligation.obstruction: The optimal-sum diameter controls support geometry but not the sum of \(K\) marginal dual sensitivities. Fixed-dimensional orthogonal tensoring saturates after at most \(d\) directions, and no declared family has an all-column reduced-cost certificate.
obligation.attempted: Subset exchanges and common-support interpolation prove the present upper bound. Hypercube parity, orthogonal, Bernoulli-knot, and two-margin constructions certify boundary cases but do not accumulate the required growing-\(K\) separation.
obligation.partial_result:
The established common-support interpolation inequality is
\[
\left|\frac{V(\mathbf Q)-V(\mathbf P)}{K^2}\right|
\le \frac1{K^2}\left|\sum_k\int\|x\|_2^2\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|
+\sum_k\sup_{g\in\mathcal C_{2(2\sqrt d+1)/K^2}}
\left|\int g\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|.
\]
Together with the optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt r\), it gives the computable uniform upper contribution \(C_d\{N^{-1/2}+\min(r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d})\}\). It does not prove that the aggregate dual fluctuation is smaller than \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\), and it supplies no simultaneous indistinguishable family.

prose_updates.tldr: The endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp uncentered causal second moment compatible with \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered variance residual. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap with Gao--Ge--Qian, the core proves a sharper empirical-MOT upper bound, the residual envelope \(r/K^2\), and optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt r\). Combining the improved term \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) with an all-estimator Bernoulli converse gives matching root-\(N\) estimation bounds whenever \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The calibrated rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}=\max\{0,\widehat L-U_{N,K}/\alpha\}\) is uniformly honest by Markov's inequality and has matching root-\(N\) minimax expected excess length in the same region. The exact estimation and one-sided length frontiers for \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), including fixed-\(K\) logarithms, remain open. The finite-support simultaneous-marginal template is defined but not instantiated: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and reduced-cost resistance to every rematching column remain explicit targets. A rational-grid primal--dual procedure separates numerical error from sampling error. The STAR audit remains conditional on known bounded scaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) plug-in calculation.

On the overlap, both analyses allow the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\) marginals, and their balanced i.i.d.-unit sampling induces this note's armwise product law. Manole--Niles-Weed leave logarithmic slack already at two margins, and no located result supplies an ordered multi-margin expected-length converse or aggregate growing-tuple dual complexity.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp residual and support-diameter geometry, the improved empirical upper rate, and matching root-\(N\) estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length for \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The honest construction is the explicit Markov-calibrated empirical-MOT plug-in lower bound. The remaining small-arm question asks whether aggregate jointly conjugate complexity improves \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) or whether a matching simultaneous lower family exists. The finite-support template is defined but not instantiated: its endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and resistance to every rematching column remain proof targets. Rational mesh, cost allowance, primal lifting, and dual shifting produce an auditable numerical bracket.

prose_updates.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same uncentered endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and prove their displayed balanced-sample plug-in rate. Comparisons here are restricted to the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class. Their published class additionally covers all dimensions and \(K\ge2\); on the overlap the distributional class is the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d.-unit design induces the armwise product law used here. The improved theorem sharpens both the residual cap and active high-dimensional term on that overlap. Manole and Niles-Weed's two-margin theorem gives the closest all-estimator nonparametric lower architecture. The two-margin reduction embeds that published subclass inside the arbitrary-margin class, so its \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) lower bound transfers upward, but it does not close the logarithmic or arm-count gap. Hundrieser, Staudt, and Munk transfer entropy between two \(c\)-conjugate potentials; no cited theorem controls the aggregate of a growing jointly conjugate \(K\)-tuple. Ji, Lei, and Spector establish broad validity from dual feasibility, while Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman study interval length for sliced Wasserstein distance; neither provides this arbitrary-margin one-sided expected-length converse. Generic discrete MOT complexity and hardness results do not preclude the fixed-dimensional squared-sum dynamic program proved here. The binary covariate-aware causal-transport papers remain informed-by comparators rather than extension targets. Mixability results for selected scalar or identical-margin classes do not settle arbitrary heterogeneous vector marginals. The STAR application comparison is conditional on the declared known-bound affine scale, i.i.d. superpopulation, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; the native unequal counts require a separate theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact small-arm frontier \(K=o(N^{q_d})\) remains open. The current estimation sandwich has nonparametric lower term \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and upper term \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\); the corresponding nonparametric ordered one-sided expected-length converse is not proved. The finite-support perturbation template has not been instantiated with endpoint separation, product-mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and nonnegative reduced cost for every rematching column. Optimal-sum diameter does not by itself bound the aggregate sensitivity of all dual potentials, while fixed-dimensional orthogonal tensoring saturates. The certified algorithm is polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\) only for fixed \(d\), and is not a generic polynomial-time exact MOT claim. Its corrected certificate uses only rational quantities \(h=1/\lceil32d/\epsilon\rceil\) and \(3dh\). The STAR audit discards observations, requires a known outcome bound and superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the native unequal-count tightening.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution preserves \(L(\mathbf P)=K^{-2}\inf_\gamma\mathbb E_\gamma\|\sum_kZ_k\|_2^2\) as an uncentered second-moment endpoint. It assumes fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced armwise product sampling, unit-ball support, and legal arrays with \(m=N/K\to\infty\), but no density or smoothness. Matching root-\(N\) bounds for estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are claimed only when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The explicit lower bound is the empirical-MOT plug-in rule calibrated by a uniform mean absolute-error allowance; no small-arm nonparametric length converse is claimed. For \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), exact rates, fixed-\(K\) logarithms, and the ordered lower family remain open. The finite-support construction is a search handle, not evidence that either a matching lower family or a sharper aggregate dual bound exists. The hypercube parity proposition remains a legal exact \(K=3,d=5\) benchmark with endpoint \(1/9\). Gao--Ge--Qian comparisons apply only on the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap; their published class is broader in \(d\) and includes \(K=2\). The STAR audit applies only to its declared balanced randomized subsample and not the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.
